clue.text: Keep causing a jam

definitions.meaning: to keep is to preserve or save from loss
a jam is a preserve of fruit boiled with sugar

explanation.definitionFit: To preserve something is to keep it, and a fruit preserve or jam carries the same name as a noun.

clue.text: Music for a trainee in domestic work

indicators.note: the word in tells us the trainee and the a go inside the household tasks

parts.note: household tasks are chores
L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a piece of music to accompany a novice doing housework.
explanation.walkthrough: A plus L (the learner, from 'trainee') goes inside CHORES; 'in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: These are hymn tunes sung by a church choir, a kind of sacred music.

clue.text: This may well be assumed by those retiring

definitions.text: This may well be assumed by those retiring

parts.words: This may well be assumed by those retiring
parts.note: assumed means put on, as clothing, and retiring means going to bed rather than leaving work

explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' suggests leaving a job and 'assumed' suggests taking for granted; both are about bedtime clothes being put on.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyjamas and nightdresses are garments people put on before going to bed.

clue.text: Returning thanks in the evening, having enjoyed dinner?

indicators.note: the word in places the turned thanks inside the poetic evening

parts.note: e'en is the poetic contraction of evening

indicators.note: returning means the word for thanks comes back to front

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: A diner says grace backwards at night after a good meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' turns the word for thanks round before it goes in; 'ta' is British slang for thanks and 'e'en' a poetic contraction of evening.
explanation.definitionFit: A meal that has been consumed with relish has been enjoyed, so the participle fits.

clue.text: Pensive perhaps, but waspish

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters of pensive may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone thoughtful may in fact be sharp-tongued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' is the anagram signal on PENSIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes things relating to wasps, the literal sense of waspish.

clue.text: Goes off for the prize

definitions.meaning: food that goes off becomes rotten or bad
booty or plunder taken by a victor

explanation.definitionFit: Food that turns rotten is said to go bad, while a victor's plunder is the loot of war.

clue.text: Fruit to snap up — Oriental fruit

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for snap is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to nip is to snap or bite
E stands for east, the Orient
an apple is a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to buy up an exotic Eastern fruit quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' turns NIP into PIN in this down clue; E is East, the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: This tropical crop with a spiky skin is a well-known fruit.

clue.text: The layabout can get riled

indicators.note: can get suggests the word riled may be turned into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A lazy person is easily annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can get' signals the anagram of RILED.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazy person who does no work is a loafer.

clue.text: Walk the street unsteady gait

parts.note: a roll is a swaying walk, like a sailor's

explanation.surface: Someone walks down the road with a wobbly step.
explanation.definitionFit: A leisurely amble is a gentle walk.

clue.text: Continue to trail a fearsome beast

parts.note: to drag is to trail along behind
on means continuing, as in carry on

explanation.surface: A frightening monster keeps dragging along behind.
explanation.definitionFit: This fire-breathing creature of legend is a terrifying monster.

clue.text: Anything tough can be changed

indicators.note: can be changed tells us the letters of tough are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Even the hardest thing can be altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can be changed' is the anagram signal on TOUGH; the answer is an old spelling of aught.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic variant of aught, meaning any thing at all.

clue.text: Money grabbed by an individual not known to be a criminal

indicators.note: grabbed by means the money is held inside the unknown person

parts.note: a stranger is a person one does not know
L stands for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: An unknown person snatches cash and turns out to be a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grabbed by' puts L (pound) inside STRANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A killer who chokes victims is a criminal.

clue.text: Coming to a sober conclusion

parts.note: TT means teetotal, so sober
an ending is a conclusion

explanation.surface: Someone is arriving at a serious, clear-headed decision.
explanation.walkthrough: TT stands for teetotal, a crossword convention for sober.
explanation.definitionFit: Being present at an event means turning up for it, so the participles match.

clue.text: "Men are —- when they woo" (A.Y.)

parts.note: Rosalind's line in As You Like It, abbreviated A.Y., likens wooing men to a spring month

explanation.walkthrough: The full line from Shakespeare's As You Like It runs 'Men are April when they woo, December when they wed'.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth month stands for fresh spring promise in the quotation.

clue.text: A solitary child before getting ahead

indicators.note: getting ahead means the word for before is placed in front of the child

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A lonely child gets ahead in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting ahead' reads like career advancement, but it only says the first piece goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit or recluse is a solitary person living apart.

clue.text: A tool for simple men to carry

indicators.note: carry means the words simple men to hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A tool easy enough for ordinary people to take around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carry' signals the letters held within 'simple men to'.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument or utensil used for a job is a tool.

clue.text: Game — the French see it and give up the ghost!

definitions.text: see it and give up the ghost

parts.note: nap is a card game
les is French for the (plural)

explanation.surface: A card game where the French player dies of shock.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the saying 'See Naples and die', meaning the Italian city is the last thing worth seeing.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says one should view this Italian city and then die.

clue.text: No longer stress there's a supplement

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
tension is stress

explanation.surface: Someone gives up being anxious once they have an added bonus.
explanation.definitionFit: An addition to a building or a deadline is a supplement.

clue.text: Many always take a long time to make purchase

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral fifty, a large number
ever means always
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: Many people always take ages to buy something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchase' means grip or mechanical advantage, not buying.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchase in the sense of a firm grip or mechanical advantage from a lever.

clue.text: Becoming a supporter with obvious hesitation

parts.note: a prop is a support
er is a spoken hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone becomes a backer while clearly dithering.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming in the sense of fitting or seemly, as appropriate behaviour.

clue.text: Somewhat sooner

definitions.meaning: preferably, as in I would sooner stay

explanation.definitionFit: The word means fairly or quite, and also expresses preference, as in 'I'd prefer'.

clue.text: The woman taking two artides to put into safe-keeping

parts.note: she is the woman
a is the indefinite article (the page's artides is an OCR slip for articles)
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A woman takes a couple of items to be stored securely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two articles' gives both A and THE, the grammatical articles.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a sword in its scabbard is to store it safely.

clue.text: Hails ship carrying a mixture of clay and cement

indicators.note: carrying means the ship holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
lute is a clay or cement used to seal joints

explanation.surface: A vessel loaded with building materials is greeted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrying' puts the other pieces inside the steamship; lute is an old word for a sealing paste of clay or cement.
explanation.definitionFit: Greetings or acknowledgements, as with a raised hand, are hails.

clue.text: The badly-bred one's trash!

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of bred and one's are jumbled

parts.note: I for one plus S for is gives one's as IS

explanation.surface: An ill-bred person's rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges BRED with IS (one is, from 'one's').
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish and scattered remains are trash.

clue.text: Proceed to prosecute on certain points

indicators.note: on means the word for prosecute is placed after the compass points

parts.note: E and N are compass points, east and north
to sue is to take legal action

explanation.surface: A lawyer moves to take someone to court on specific counts.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means placed after; 'certain points' are compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow on or result is to proceed.

clue.text: Spoke about the little page being most pleasant

definitions.note: the setter loosely stretches the sense to a superlative

indicators.note: about means the word for spoke goes around the page

parts.note: said is spoke
p is the short form of page

explanation.surface: Someone talked of the small page boy being delightful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' places P (page) inside SAID.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means savoury or full of flavour, so agreeable to taste.

clue.text: To make cuts, the king is content to show patience

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: is content means the king is held inside the word for making cuts

parts.note: to lance is to cut open
ER is Edward Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: A ruler is happy to perform surgery calmly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is content' (contained) puts ER inside LANCE; ER here stands for Edward Rex, a king.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience and forbearance mean putting up with things.

clue.text: Note a villain's come round repeatedly

parts.note: re is a note of the sol-fa scale
a cur is a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A rogue keeps returning.
explanation.definitionFit: To happen again and again is to come round repeatedly.

clue.text: Right now framing egghead's picture

indicators.note: framing means the head of egg sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: R is right
present means now
the head of egg is its first letter

explanation.surface: Right now an intellectual's portrait is being framed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Framing' places E (the head of 'egg') inside R plus PRESENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To depict or portray something is to picture it.

clue.text: Feature a Far-Eastern country

parts.note: a chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: Someone describes an Asian nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The People's Republic in East Asia is a country.

clue.text: Teased unrestrainedly for appearing cool

indicators.note: unrestrainedly signals the letters of teased run free into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone mocked mercilessly stays unruffled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unrestrainedly' is the anagram signal on TEASED.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm and composed manner equals cool.

clue.text: Part friends?

parts.note: to part friends means to make them separate, not part of a group of friends

explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' looks like a noun but is a verb: to separate friends.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate people is to drive them apart.
